# Company 105 — Global Trade & Customs Compliance Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:105`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:105`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-105-v2.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Roadmap conformance:** EXHAUSTIVE 28-PASS / A–BZ MAPPED; saturation subject to portfolio reverse-map reconciliation  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customs filing, export declaration, restricted-party decision, tariff payment, broker instruction, shipment release, license application, paid data subscription, outreach, deployment or public launch.  
**First-class project requirement:** independent Command Center project button, independently computed percentage, independent project pages, Brain/Agent/service state, evidence/checkpoints, Needs Me, incidents, approvals, dependencies and lifecycle.

## Business identity

Purpose: automate intelligence and administrative workflows for lawful cross-border trade while preserving legal, customs-broker, export-control, sanctions, licensing and human-review boundaries.

Core problem: international trade requires product classification, valuation, origin, trade-agreement eligibility, duties/taxes, sanctions/restricted-party screening, export controls, licenses, documentation, broker coordination and constantly changing country-specific rules. Manual processes are fragmented across spreadsheets, brokers, government portals, ERP data and supplier attestations, creating cost, delay and compliance risk.

Value proposition: a versioned evidence-centered trade operating layer that turns product, party, supplier and shipment data into traceable classification/origin/landed-cost/compliance workflows, continuously monitors regulatory changes and escalates ambiguity or protected determinations to qualified personnel.

Non-goal: not autonomous legal advice, not a customs broker of record by default, not an exporter/importer of record, and not an unattended authority to release restricted goods, evade duties, bypass sanctions or misstate origin/value.

## Complete product tree

Product Master & Trade Data Hub; HS/HTS Classification Assistant; Classification Rationale/Evidence; Binding-Ruling/Decision Reference Manager; Commodity Code Crosswalk; Export Classification/ECCN Support; Dual-Use/Product Control Analysis; Country-of-Origin Engine; Rules-of-Origin Engine; Free-Trade-Agreement Qualification; Supplier Origin Solicitation; Bill-of-Materials Origin Analysis; Regional Value Content Calculator; Tariff/Duty Engine; Trade Remedy Engine; Anti-Dumping/Countervailing Duty Support; Quota/Embargo Rule Monitor; Customs Valuation Engine; Transfer-Price/Assist/Royalty Valuation Support; Landed Cost Calculator; VAT/GST/Import Tax Estimation; De Minimis Rules; Restricted/Denied Party Screening; Sanctions Screening; Embargo/Country Restriction Screening; End-Use/End-User Risk Support; Export License Requirement Support; License/Permit Workflow; Import Permit Workflow; Documentation Generator; Commercial Invoice/Packing/Origin Document Support; Declaration Data Pack; Broker Collaboration Portal; Shipment Compliance Gate; Customs Entry Audit; Post-Entry/Correction Support; Recordkeeping Vault; Drawback/Duty Recovery Support where applicable; Foreign Trade Zone/Bonded Workflow Support; Product Compliance Cross-Reference; Trade Policy Monitor; Regulatory Change Impact Engine; Supply-Chain Route/Trade Optimization; ERP/TMS/WMS Integration; Customs Broker API; Tariff API; Classification API; Landed-Cost API; Screening API; Enterprise Multi-Country Console; Private Deployment; White-Label/OEM Infrastructure.

## Complete feature tree

SKU/product identity; description; material/composition; function/use; manufacturing process; technical specifications; HS/HTS/ECCN candidate; rationale; evidence; jurisdiction; effective date; duty rate; additional duties/remedies; origin; substantial transformation facts; BOM/source countries; FTA rule; qualification evidence; valuation method; transaction value; assists; royalties; freight/insurance; currency; Incoterm; importer/exporter; consignee; end user; parties; screening result; license/permit; country restrictions; quota; shipment route; entry/declaration data; broker status; customs response; audit finding; correction; document version; regulatory source/version; human decision; confidence; expiry; audit trail.

## Complete customer tree

Importers; exporters; manufacturers; ecommerce sellers; marketplaces; distributors; wholesalers; retailers; logistics providers; freight forwarders; customs brokers; 3PLs; supply-chain organizations; industrial companies; electronics; automotive; apparel; consumer goods; chemicals where lawful; medical-device manufacturers; food businesses; aerospace/defense-adjacent organizations where lawful and with stricter controls; software/hardware vendors; enterprise procurement; trade-compliance consultancies; ERP/TMS vendors.

## Complete vertical tree

Consumer goods; apparel/textiles; electronics; machinery; automotive; industrial components; chemicals; food/agriculture; medical devices; pharmaceuticals supply-chain administration; aerospace; energy; ecommerce parcels; marketplace imports; cross-border DTC; wholesale distribution; spare parts; luxury goods; raw materials; software/hardware bundles. Each vertical requires product ontology and regulatory/jurisdiction packs.

## Specialized Brain capability tree

The Global Trade Brain must KNOW HS/HTS structures, explanatory/reference materials where licensed/public, customs valuation concepts, origin/rules of origin, trade agreements, export controls, sanctions/restricted-party concepts, licenses, quotas, embargoes, import/export documentation and country-specific regulatory structures. It must UNDERSTAND product facts, supply chain, transaction context and rule effective dates; CLASSIFY products/parties/controls; REASON about classification/origin/valuation/FTA requirements; PLAN evidence collection and filing support; PREDICT duty/lead-time/risk as assistive analytics; OPTIMIZE lawful sourcing/routing/landed cost; RECOMMEND candidates with evidence; VERIFY rule/source/version; EXPLAIN rationale and uncertainty; ESCALATE ambiguous or high-impact determinations.

The Brain must distinguish candidate classification from approved classification, source law/regulation from guidance, deterministic screen match from identity uncertainty, and commercial optimization from legal eligibility.

## Brain architecture

Brain Factory base + global-trade domain pack + jurisdiction/country packs + product/commodity ontology + tariff/control-rule graph + trade-agreement/rules-of-origin graph + party/sanctions evidence layer + deterministic calculators/rule engine + regulatory source/effective-date registry + human trade-compliance approval layer.

Memory: company/tenant isolated product classification/origin history; versioned decision rationale; supplier evidence; no cross-customer confidential BOM/sourcing reuse by default.

Evaluations: HS/ECCN candidate accuracy; classification explanation/source faithfulness; origin/rules-of-origin reasoning; duty calculation; valuation completeness; screening match accuracy; regulatory freshness; unsupported legal claim rate; stale-rate detection; cross-tenant leakage; document/prompt injection; escalation correctness; landed-cost reconciliation.

## Complete Agent tree

Product Data Agent; Classification Agent; Export Classification Agent; Origin Agent; FTA Agent; Supplier Evidence Agent; Valuation Agent; Duty/Tariff Agent; Trade Remedy Agent; Landed Cost Agent; Restricted Party Agent; Sanctions Agent; Export Control Agent; License/Permit Agent; Documentation Agent; Broker Coordination Agent; Shipment Compliance Agent; Entry Audit Agent; Regulatory Change Agent; Recordkeeping Agent; Duty Recovery Agent; ERP Integration Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Independent QA Agent.

No agent independently misdeclares goods, approves sanctions/export-control exceptions, signs customs declarations, instructs shipment release or commits funds without the appropriate authorization and qualified review.

## Deterministic / non-agent services

Tariff table lookup; rate/effective-date engine; currency conversion; duty/tax calculation; regional value content math; BOM aggregation; origin rule evaluation where codified; restricted-party exact/fuzzy matching; country embargo matrix; Incoterm cost allocation; valuation calculators; unit conversions; document schema validation; required-field checks; identifier normalization; country/code crosswalks; audit logging; record retention; idempotent workflow; deadline calendars; webhook/EDI transforms; data reconciliation.

## Input tree

Product descriptions; specifications; images/documents; material composition; BOM; part numbers; supplier data; manufacturing steps; origin attestations; purchase/sales transactions; prices; assists/royalties; Incoterms; freight/insurance; party identities; addresses; destination/origin countries; end-use/end-user data; sanctions/restricted lists; licenses; trade agreements; tariff/control tables; customs rulings/guidance; broker responses; shipment/entry records; regulatory updates.

## Output tree

Classification candidates and approved record; ECCN/control candidate; origin determination support; FTA qualification/evidence pack; tariff/duty estimate; landed cost; valuation checklist/calculation; screening findings; license/permit requirement support; shipment compliance checklist; document/declaration data pack; broker instruction draft; audit exception; regulatory change alert; product impact list; recordkeeping bundle; management analytics; API responses.

## Workflow tree

Authorize company/jurisdiction → create product/trade master → collect product/BOM/supplier evidence → classify product → verify export controls → determine origin/FTA → establish valuation inputs → screen parties/countries/end use → determine permits/licenses → calculate duties/taxes/landed cost → assemble documents/declaration data → qualified review where required → broker/authorized filing handoff → monitor customs response/shipment → reconcile actual vs estimated duties/entry → handle correction/audit → retain evidence → monitor rule changes and re-evaluate affected products.

## Integration tree

ERP; PLM; PIM; procurement; supplier portals; TMS; WMS; ecommerce/marketplaces; order management; freight forwarders; customs brokers; EDI; government trade/customs portals/APIs where permitted; sanctions/restricted-party data sources; tariff databases; trade agreement sources; document management; finance/accounting; payment/tax systems; SSO; data warehouse/BI; SIEM; secure messaging.

## API / developer ecosystem

Classification API; tariff/rate API; origin/FTA API; valuation API; landed-cost API; party-screening API; export-control API; license workflow API; document/declaration-data API; regulatory-change API; audit/provenance API; connector SDK; sandbox product/shipment fixtures; webhook/event API; versioned jurisdiction packs.

## Data architecture

Tenant-isolated product/trade master; classification decision history; tariff/control rule graph; origin/BOM graph; supplier evidence store; party screening records; licenses/permits; shipment/entry events; document refs; regulatory source registry; effective-date/version metadata; immutable audit/evidence ledger; region/residency controls; secrets isolated from business data; backup/recovery.

## Data moat

Potential moat: normalized tariff/control/origin rule graph, product ontology, verified classification decision patterns, supplier evidence workflows, broker/customs interoperability, regulatory change mapping and de-identified authorized exception/accuracy benchmarks. Never pool confidential customer BOM/sourcing/party data without permission.

## IP

Trade rule/effective-date graph; product-to-classification evidence model; origin/BOM qualification engine; trade-change impact graph; valuation completeness engine; landed-cost reconciliation; jurisdiction pack framework; classification evaluation corpus; broker/document interoperability layer.

## Monetization

Per SKU/product classification; per shipment/entry; per screen; per landed-cost calculation; subscription; seats; enterprise/multi-country license; API usage; supplier module; audit/compliance module; private deployment; white-label/OEM; managed trade data operations where contractually appropriate. No revenue promise.

## Packaging

Tariff/classification starter; origin/FTA; screening/export control; landed cost/valuation; shipment/document compliance; trade audit; regulatory monitor; full global trade OS; enterprise multi-country; API/OEM/private deployment.

## Distribution

ERP/TMS/PLM partnerships; customs/logistics ecosystem; enterprise trade/compliance procurement; ecommerce platforms; brokers/forwarder technology partners; developer/API channels. No outreach authorized now.

## Acquisition automation

Future inbound qualification may map countries, product volume, categories, shipment volume, ERP/TMS and compliance scope to a technical fit. It may not provide binding legal classifications, commercial outreach, sign terms or initiate filings.

## Customer lifecycle

Trade-data assessment → jurisdiction/vertical mapping → integrations → product-master cleanup → sandbox classification/rule calibration → qualified review baseline → controlled rollout → shipment/document integration → audit/reconciliation → expansion to countries/modules → renewal/export/offboarding.

## Support / customer success

Classification disputes; rule/source questions; supplier-origin gaps; screening false positives; broker integration; customs response; duty variance; regulatory change; outage/incident; audit evidence. Success measures cycle time, data completeness, reconciliation, manual effort and exception reduction—not guaranteed customs clearance.

## Automation maximum / human-intervention minimum

Automate data ingestion, deterministic rate math, rule monitoring, evidence collection, screening triage, documentation assembly, supplier requests, impact analysis and routine reconciliation. Retain qualified humans for ambiguous classification/origin/valuation, sanctions/export-control decisions, legal interpretation, declarations/attestations, licenses and high-impact disputes.

## Operations / administration

Jurisdiction/source updates; product/rule data quality; supplier evidence; broker/provider credentials; integration health; screening lists; license calendars; records retention; audit support; billing; support; incident response; backup/recovery; vendor/source licensing; model/rule versioning.

## Security

Protect supplier, BOM, pricing, party and shipment data; tenant isolation; encryption; least privilege; SSO/MFA; secrets vault; secure broker/government connections; signed rule/source updates; DLP; egress controls; document scanning; model/tool permission limits; audit; key rotation; incident response; supply-chain security.

## Privacy

Minimize personal party/contact data; purpose limitation; retention; sanctions screening evidence controls; cross-border data transfer/residency; access logging; deletion/export where lawful; no unauthorized reuse of supplier/customer data.

## Compliance

Adapt to customs, import/export, sanctions, export controls, trade remedies, product-specific restrictions, recordkeeping and jurisdiction requirements. Actual legal obligations vary by country/product/party and require qualified review. Roadmap work does not establish broker status or regulatory certification.

## Legal

Customs broker/importer/exporter-of-record responsibilities; tariff/classification law; export-control/sanctions law; trade agreements; licenses; product regulation; data-source licenses; broker terms; recordkeeping; confidentiality/IP; liability; audit; government portal terms. Legal determinations remain governed.

## Abuse / misuse

Prevent deliberate misclassification, undervaluation, origin laundering, sanctions evasion, export-control circumvention, false supplier attestations, document fabrication, shipment splitting intended to evade rules, restricted-party probing, credential misuse and rule-source tampering.

## Reliability

Versioned tariff/control sources; effective-date correctness; idempotent calculations/workflows; deterministic math; source freshness alarms; provider/broker outage handling; retries/dead letters; reconciliation actual vs predicted; manual fallback; no auto-clearance on missing rule data; backup/restore; DR.

## Observability

Product classifications; unresolved classifications; rule freshness; screening results; supplier evidence age; FTA qualification; duty estimates vs actual; landed-cost variance; document completeness; broker/API health; shipment exceptions; license deadlines; model confidence; human overrides; cost per transaction; security incidents.

## Incident response

Critical incidents: stale/misapplied tariff/control rule at scale, false sanctions clear, cross-tenant product/BOM leak, wrong mass classification, valuation error, compromised broker/government credential, duplicate/incorrect declaration support. Stop affected automation, preserve evidence, identify impacted products/shipments, notify authorized owners, recalculate/rescreen, rollback rule/model version and remediate.

## Testing

Known classification/ruling corpus; tariff effective-date tests; origin/FTA scenarios; BOM/RVC calculations; valuation cases; sanctions/restricted-party matching; country/control rules; document schemas; broker/API contract tests; idempotency; source outage/staleness; permission/isolation; prompt/document injection; DR; load/performance; reconciliation against known entries.

## Brain evaluations

Classification candidate precision/recall; rationale/source citation; origin reasoning; FTA rule interpretation; valuation completeness; export-control support; screening identity match; regulatory freshness; unsupported legal conclusion rate; escalation; leakage; tool-use authorization; landed-cost accuracy.

## Deployment

Isolated dev/test/staging/production; jurisdiction/data-source version pinning; signed releases; feature flags; canary by country/customer/product family; schema migration gates; rollback; private enterprise options; region controls. No production deployment authorized now.

## Scale

Single importer/product catalog → multi-country enterprise → global supply chain → broker/marketplace embedded infrastructure. Scale product graph, rule engine, screens, supplier workflow, shipment events and document generation independently.

## Performance

Interactive classification/screen/landed-cost seconds when data ready; large catalogs and regulatory re-evaluation asynchronous; shipment gates predictable. Cache tariff/control data only with effective-date/freshness correctness.

## Cost

Licensed tariff/screening/regulatory data; model inference; document extraction; integrations; storage/audit; screening volume; support/compliance. Track cost per SKU/screen/shipment/entry and repeated paid dependencies for internalization analysis; no spend authorized now.

## Financial metrics

ARR/MRR if later real; revenue per SKU/shipment/screen/API; source/vendor cost; gross margin; classification/support labor; implementation cost; duty variance/recovery where legitimately measured; retention/expansion. No test revenue.

## Moat

Trade rule/effective-date graph; classification evidence corpus; product ontology; origin/BOM engine; supplier evidence network; broker interoperability; regulatory change impact; reconciliation accuracy.

## Network effects

More public rule mappings, connector coverage and non-private product-taxonomy evidence can improve service. Customer-specific classifications/BOMs stay isolated unless explicitly authorized for reuse.

## Platform

Can become a global trade operating layer coordinating product data, rules, parties, suppliers, shipments, brokers, documentation, audits and optimization.

## White label / OEM

ERP/TMS/ecommerce/logistics/customs technology providers may embed tariff, classification, landed-cost, screening and compliance modules. Responsibility and approved classification ownership remain explicit.

## Internationalization

Internationalization is foundational: country-specific tariff schedules, customs valuation nuances, origin rules, FTAs, taxes, export controls, sanctions, language, currencies, units, documentation and portals require versioned jurisdiction packs.

## Accessibility

Accessible classification/review/admin interfaces; keyboard/screen-reader use; clear source/rationale; non-color-only risk alerts; accessible documents and tables; understandable errors.

## Mobile

Mobile for shipment alerts, approvals, supplier evidence capture and status. Complex classification/audit work remains desktop-friendly; strong device/session controls required.

## Voice

Potential secure status/search/warehouse or broker-note capture. Never accept voice alone for protected declarations or high-impact legal determinations without governed authentication/approval.

## Multimodal

Product images, spec sheets, labels, certificates, invoices and shipment documents can enrich classification/evidence. Extracted attributes need source/confidence and human verification where material.

## Marketplace

Future certified jurisdiction packs, broker/logistics connectors, supplier evidence modules and product ontologies. Third-party modules require signing, sandboxing, data scopes and evaluation.

## Developer ecosystem

APIs/SDKs; sandbox SKUs/shipments; jurisdiction pack interface; connector SDK; rule-test harness; webhooks; versioned schemas; deprecation; certification.

## Partners

ERP/TMS/PLM vendors; customs brokers; freight/logistics platforms; tariff/screening data providers; trade consultants; ecommerce/marketplace platforms. Planning only, no outreach.

## Training / certification

Trade-data administrator; classification reviewer; origin/FTA analyst; broker integration; compliance/security; jurisdiction pack; API developer training. Any professional certification claims require actual program later.

## Community

Future non-confidential trade-data/product-classification community could contribute public references and integration knowledge under moderation. No customer proprietary trade data sharing by default.

## Content / knowledge

Jurisdiction guides; source/effective-date notes; classification methodology; origin/FTA playbooks; valuation checklists; export-control workflows; broker integration docs; audit/reconciliation runbooks; release/change notes.

## Experimentation

Historical/synthetic trade data first; shadow classifications; compare rule/model versions; human-reviewed experiments; never silently change approved classifications, sanctions thresholds or live filing data.

## Continuous improvement

Learn from customs/broker responses, reviewer overrides, duty variance, supplier evidence failures and regulation changes. Update evaluation sets and compatibility profiles; governed promotion only.

## Spinoffs

Tariff API; classification engine; landed-cost API; origin/FTA engine; trade-policy monitor; supplier-origin network; broker integration layer could become products or eventual companies only if new-company test passes.

## Cross-sell

Adjacent companies: KYC/KYB screening, logistics optimization, supplier risk, pricing intelligence, ecommerce, tax compliance, document automation, data lineage. Keep company projects distinct.

## Bundling

Classification + tariff; origin/FTA; export controls/screening; landed cost/valuation; shipment/document compliance; full trade OS; enterprise/private/OEM.

## Failures

Bad product data; wrong HS/ECCN; stale tariff; origin evidence missing; FTA misqualification; valuation omission; sanctions false negative/positive; license missed; quota/embargo change; wrong Incoterm allocation; currency error; broker API outage; government portal outage; duplicate data; document mismatch; rule conflict.

## Edge cases

Multi-function products; kits/sets; software+hardware; returned goods; repairs; temporary imports; samples; free-of-charge goods; assists/royalties; related-party valuation; transformation across many countries; mixed-origin BOM; tariff engineering; dual-use items; transshipment; special economic zones; drawback; bonded goods; country changes mid-shipment; retroactive rule changes.

## Kill / safe mode

Per country/source/rule/model/agent/shipment kill switch; freeze automated clearance recommendation; force human review; disable compromised screening source; stop document/declaration output; revert tariff/control dataset; revoke broker credential; read-only audit mode.

## Exit / portability

Export product/trade master, classification/origin rationale, source versions, supplier evidence, screening records, licenses, shipment/entry history, documents and audit trail in documented formats; revoke integrations; retain/delete per law/contract.

## Scale vision

Classification/landed-cost tool → importer/exporter trade OS → global enterprise trade platform → embedded customs/trade infrastructure for marketplaces/logistics/ERP ecosystems.

## Autonomous mature state

Routine data ingestion, rate math, source monitoring, supplier evidence collection, screening, document assembly and reconciliation run automatically. Qualified humans retain ambiguous classification/origin/valuation, export-control/sanctions, licensing, declarations and dispute authority. Every recommendation is versioned, sourced and auditable.

## Command Center dependencies

First-class project/button/progress/pages; Brain/Agent factories; Capability/Integration registries; identity/tenant; data governance; security/privacy/authorization; rule/effective-date engine; graph; document/multimodal intelligence; browser/API workers; secrets; testing/evaluation; observability/incident/recovery; resource/financial governors; approval/Needs Me; audit/provenance/versioning.

## Retrofit risk

If Command Center lacks source/effective-date versioning, deterministic rule/calculation services, jurisdiction packs, evidence/provenance, protected-action gates and large catalog re-evaluation, trade compliance would force costly retrofits later.

## Phased roadmap

Phase 0 architecture/public/synthetic corpus → Phase 1 tariff/classification + product master → Phase 2 origin/FTA + supplier evidence → Phase 3 valuation/landed cost → Phase 4 screening/export controls/license workflows → Phase 5 documents/broker/shipment/audit → Phase 6 enterprise multi-country → Phase 7 API/OEM/private → Phase 8 governed optimization/internalization.

## Reuse candidates

Identity/tenant; rule/effective-date engine; graph; document extraction; screening matcher; workflow/queues; source monitoring; audit/provenance; browser/API integration; data quality; currency/unit services; observability; incident/recovery; evaluation; versioning.

## Proven capability dependencies

Generic reusable components require trade-specific compatibility and regulatory evaluation. Critical screening/rule/calculation/document services need proof maturity, version pinning, staged rollout and rollback before broad sharing.

## Company-specific capabilities

HS/HTS/ECCN taxonomy; trade rule graph; origin/FTA/BOM engine; customs valuation; trade remedies/quotas; broker/declaration data model; jurisdiction packs; trade evaluation corpus.

## External dependencies to internalize

Generic candidates: document extraction, rules, source monitoring, screening matching, workflow, browser/API orchestration, data quality and landed-cost math. Official tariff/customs/sanctions/regulatory sources and licensed databases may remain external with portability and provenance.

## Blast-radius requirements

Critical/high: mass wrong classification/rate, sanctions/export-control false clearance, wrong valuation, compromised government/broker credential, shared stale rule source. Enforce tenant/country scoping, source pinning, canaries, reconciliation and kill/rollback.

## Version / compatibility requirements

Version tariff schedules, controls, sanctions lists, agreements, origin rules, valuation rules, Brain, agent, classification record, source, API, connector and document schema. Preserve effective dates and reproducibility of prior decisions.

acceptanceCriteria:
Original section Business identity (source line 11):
Purpose: automate intelligence and administrative workflows for lawful cross-border trade while preserving legal, customs-broker, export-control, sanctions, licensing and human-review boundaries.

Core problem: international trade requires product classification, valuation, origin, trade-agreement eligibility, duties/taxes, sanctions/restricted-party screening, export controls, licenses, documentation, broker coordination and constantly changing country-specific rules. Manual processes are fragmented across spreadsheets, brokers, government portals, ERP data and supplier attestations, creating cost, delay and compliance risk.

Value proposition: a versioned evidence-centered trade operating layer that turns product, party, supplier and shipment data into traceable classification/origin/landed-cost/compliance workflows, continuously monitors regulatory changes and escalates ambiguity or protected determinations to qualified personnel.

Non-goal: not autonomous legal advice, not a customs broker of record by default, not an exporter/importer of record, and not an unattended authority to release restricted goods, evade duties, bypass sanctions or misstate origin/value.

workUnits.title: Reconcile and implement Exhaustive 28-pass findings
acceptanceCriteria:
Original section Exhaustive 28-pass findings (source line 325):
1. Core Business — coherent global trade/customs operating layer with professional/legal boundaries.
2. Product Expansion — classification, origin, valuation, screening, licenses, documents, audit, APIs and enterprise mapped.
3. Customer Expansion — importers/exporters/manufacturers/ecommerce/logistics/brokers/software mapped.
4. Industry / Vertical Expansion — product/industry packs and jurisdiction packs mapped.
5. Specialized Brain — full trade-domain Brain justified.
6. Agent Decomposition — classification/origin/valuation/screening/license/broker/audit agents mapped.
7. Deterministic Services — tariff math, RVC, rules, screening, currencies, schemas mapped.
8. Data Products — tariff/regulatory intelligence and non-private benchmarks possible.
9. API / Developer Products — tariff/classification/origin/landed-cost/screening APIs mapped.
10. White Label / OEM / Embedded — strong ERP/TMS/ecommerce/logistics fit.
11. Enterprise — multi-country, large catalog, SSO, private deployment, governance mapped.
12. Marketplace / Platform — certified country packs/connectors/product ontologies possible later.
13. Monetization — SKU/shipment/screen/subscription/API/enterprise mapped.
14. Distribution — ERP/logistics/broker/ecommerce/procurement channels mapped.
15. Automation — routine data/rules/docs/monitoring/reconciliation highly automatable.
16. Human-Intervention Elimination — reduce repetitive admin, retain ambiguous/protected determinations.
17. Moats — rule graph, classification evidence, origin/BOM, supplier interoperability, reconciliation mapped.
18. Security — sensitive supplier/pricing/party/credential controls mapped.
19. Privacy — party/contact/supplier-data minimization and cross-border data controls mapped.
20. Compliance — customs/export/sanctions/records framework adaptability mapped.
21. Failure / Edge Cases — special procedures, valuation, kits, returns, dual-use, retroactivity mapped.
22. Internationalization — foundational country-specific design mapped.
23. Scale — catalog/country/shipment/source partitioning mapped.
24. Future Technology — better digital customs APIs, product passports and machine-readable rules can deepen automation.
25. Cross-Company Synergy — screening, rule engine, docs, source monitoring, graph reusable.
26. Spinoffs — tariff/classification/origin/landed-cost/trade monitor candidates mapped.
27. Adversarial Missing-Idea Pass — added trade remedies, bonded/FTZ/drawback, related-party valuation, end-use, retroactive rules, customs audit/corrections.
28. Saturation Pass — remaining branches fit jurisdiction/product/procedure packs or adjacent companies; Company 105 remains coherent.

Independently verify real project-scoped artifacts, failure paths, source rights, owner boundaries and $0 compliance. Planning, simulated work, and registry rows are never evidence of an operational executor.

# Company 106 — Insurance Claims Automation & Claims Intelligence Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:106`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:106`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-106-v2.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Roadmap conformance:** EXHAUSTIVE 28-PASS / A–BZ MAPPED; saturation subject to portfolio reverse-map reconciliation  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no claim adjudication, coverage denial, settlement, reserve change, payment, fraud accusation, policyholder contact, provider assignment, customer onboarding, paid data access, deployment or public launch.  
**First-class project requirement:** independent Command Center project button, independently computed percentage, independent project pages, Brain/Agent/service state, evidence/checkpoints, Needs Me, incidents, approvals, dependencies and lifecycle.

## Business identity

Purpose: digitize and intelligently coordinate insurance claim workflows from first notice through evidence, triage, investigation support, estimating, communications, settlement support, payment workflow, subrogation, closure and reopening while preserving insurer policy, regulatory, contractual and human decision boundaries.

Core problem: claims operations combine policy interpretation, claimant identity, incident evidence, documents, photos/video, estimates, providers, fraud indicators, reserves, communications, legal/regulatory deadlines, payment and recovery. Fragmented systems and manual handoffs slow resolution and create inconsistent service, leakage and audit risk.

Value proposition: an evidence-centered claims operating layer that automates intake, normalization, document/media understanding, workflow routing, routine task execution, provider coordination, quality checks and analytics while keeping consequential coverage, fraud, liability, settlement and payment authority with properly authorized insurer personnel or rules.

Non-goal: not an autonomous insurer, adjuster, attorney or medical evaluator; not a system that independently denies claims, accuses fraud, makes binding settlement decisions or pays money without explicit policy and authorization.

## Complete product tree

FNOL Intake; Claim Creation; Policy/Insured Verification; Coverage Data Retrieval; Coverage Issue Workbench; Claimant/Party Registry; Incident/Exposure Registry; Evidence Upload; Document Intelligence; Photo/Video Damage Intelligence; Audio/Call Intelligence; Geospatial/Weather/Event Enrichment; Vehicle/Property/Asset Data Enrichment; Triage Engine; Severity Estimation Support; Fraud Indicator Engine; Special Investigation Referral Support; Liability Fact Organizer; Assignment/Routing; Adjuster Workbench; Provider/Vendor Routing; Repair Network Coordination; Medical-Bill/Document Administration where applicable; Estimate Intake; Estimate Comparison; Repair Scope Comparison; Total-Loss Support; Catastrophe Event Intake; Bulk/CAT Claim Processing; Communication Orchestration; Status Updates; Task/Diary Management; Reserve Recommendation Support; Coverage/Limit/Excess Tracking; Settlement Recommendation Support; Authority-Level Routing; Payment Workflow; Recovery/Salvage Support; Subrogation Support; Recovery Demand Administration; Litigation Handoff Support; Complaint/Regulatory Deadline Tracker; QA/File Review; Leakage/Variance Analytics; Claim Outcome Analytics; Provider Performance; Fraud Trend Analytics; Reopening Workflow; Claim Audit/Evidence Vault; Insurer API; TPA API; Embedded/White-Label Claims Infrastructure; Enterprise Multi-Line Console; Private Deployment; Line-of-Business Packs.

## Complete feature tree

Claim/policy IDs; claimant/insured; parties/roles; incident date/time/location; loss cause; line of business; coverage/limit/deductible refs; exposure types; evidence files; document types; photo/video objects; damage regions; estimate line items; provider/vendor; assignment; adjuster; tasks/deadlines; severity score; fraud indicators; confidence; liability facts; coverage issues; reserve recommendation; authority level; communication history; offer/settlement candidate; payment status; recovery/subrogation; salvage; catastrophe/event link; legal/complaint flags; human decisions; source/evidence citations; model/rule version; audit state; reopening reason.

## Complete customer tree

Property/casualty insurers; auto insurers; homeowners/renters insurers; commercial insurers; specialty insurers; travel insurers; pet insurers; marine insurers; workers-compensation claims administrators where appropriate; TPAs; MGAs; self-insured enterprises; claims service providers; repair networks; restoration networks; insurance software vendors; reinsurer-adjacent claim analytics users where permitted; government insurance programs where authorized.

## Complete vertical tree

Auto physical damage; auto liability; homeowners property; renters; commercial property; general liability; travel; pet; marine; specialty property/casualty; workers compensation administration; catastrophe property; small commercial; warranty/service-contract claims where sufficiently analogous. Each requires line-specific policy, evidence, estimating, regulatory and evaluation packs.

## Specialized Brain capability tree

The Claims Intelligence Brain must KNOW claim lifecycles, insurance operations, policy/coverage data structures, evidence types, damage concepts, estimates, provider workflows, fraud indicators, reserves, subrogation and regulatory timing. It must UNDERSTAND incident context and evidence provenance; CLASSIFY claim/exposure/document/damage/task/risk; REASON about missing information, workflow routing and inconsistencies; PLAN claim tasks; PREDICT severity/duration/leakage/fraud risk only as assistive analytics; FORECAST queues/CAT demand; OPTIMIZE assignment/provider/task sequencing; RECOMMEND next steps with evidence; VERIFY consistency/calculations; EXPLAIN findings; ESCALATE high-impact coverage, fraud, settlement, medical/legal or payment decisions.

The Brain must distinguish policy data, claimant allegation, third-party statement, evidence, model inference, adjuster conclusion and binding insurer decision.

## Brain architecture

Brain Factory base + insurance claims domain pack + line-of-business packs + policy/product schema layer + claim evidence graph + multimodal damage/document layer + provider/estimate model + deterministic coverage/limit/calculation services + workflow planner + fraud/severity analytics + human authority/approval policy.

Memory is insurer/tenant and claim scoped. Private claim information does not become cross-customer memory by default. Model outputs retain source, confidence, version and review state.

Evaluations: FNOL extraction; document classification; damage detection; estimate comparison; claim routing; severity prediction calibration; fraud-indicator precision/recall without unsupported accusation; source faithfulness; policy/coverage data handling; reserve/settlement recommendation calibration where used; communication safety; cross-tenant leakage; bias/fairness; image/document manipulation; prompt injection; escalation correctness.

## Complete Agent tree

FNOL Agent; Policy Data Agent; Party/Identity Agent; Evidence Intake Agent; Document Agent; Photo/Video Damage Agent; Triage Agent; Severity Agent; Fraud Indicator Agent; Assignment Agent; Adjuster Support Agent; Estimate Agent; Provider Routing Agent; Communication Agent; Task/Diary Agent; Reserve Support Agent; Settlement Support Agent; Payment Workflow Agent; Subrogation Agent; Salvage/Recovery Agent; CAT Response Agent; Complaint/Deadline Agent; QA/File Review Agent; Analytics Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Independent Claims QA Agent; Incident/Reconciliation Agent.

Agents act within explicit authority ceilings. Coverage denial, fraud determination, binding settlement, material reserve authority, payment release and legal/medical judgments remain protected unless a narrowly defined insurer-owned deterministic rule and authorization explicitly permits automation.

## Deterministic / non-agent services

Policy/claim schema validation; limit/deductible arithmetic; date/deadline calendars; payment math; tax/depreciation calculation where codified; estimate line-item normalization; duplicate claim/evidence detection; geocoding; weather/event lookup adapters; provider eligibility rules; authority-level routing; workflow state machine; document hashing; audit logging; idempotency; payment reconciliation; communication preference/consent rules; retention; encryption/key management; queues/retries/dead letters; backup/restore.

## Input tree

FNOL forms/calls/messages; policy/coverage data; claimant/insured/third-party data; incident descriptions; police/fire reports; photos/video; repair/property estimates; invoices/receipts; medical/admin documents where applicable; witness statements; telemetry where lawfully available; weather/geospatial data; vehicle/property data; provider records; adjuster notes; fraud signals; payment data; litigation/subrogation documents; complaints; prior claim history where lawful and authorized; human decisions.

## Output tree

Structured claim; missing-information checklist; evidence summary; damage/estimate findings; triage/severity recommendation; fraud-indicator report; assignment task; provider route; communication draft/status; claim diary; reserve support; settlement support; payment instruction candidate; subrogation/recovery lead; CAT prioritization; QA exceptions; leakage/variance analytics; audit evidence; API/webhook events; human-review tasks.

## Workflow tree

Receive FNOL → verify policy/party/incident → create claim/exposures → collect evidence → classify documents/media → identify coverage/data issues for authorized review → triage severity/risk → route adjuster/provider → gather estimates/evidence → compare/QA → investigate inconsistencies/fraud indicators → maintain communications/tasks/deadlines → generate reserve/settlement support → route by authority → approved payment workflow → recovery/subrogation/salvage → QA/audit → close → monitor reopening triggers → reopen with preserved history when authorized.

## Integration tree

Policy administration; claims core systems; CRM/contact center; telephony; email/SMS/secure messaging; document management; mobile capture; repair estimating platforms; repair/restoration/provider networks; payment systems; fraud/data vendors; weather/geospatial; vehicle/property data; medical-bill networks where appropriate; legal/litigation systems; reinsurance/data warehouses; SSO; SIEM; accounting; regulatory/complaint systems.

## API / developer ecosystem

FNOL API; claim API; evidence/document/media API; damage-intelligence API; triage/severity API; fraud-indicator API; estimate-comparison API; provider-routing API; communication/status API; payment-workflow API; subrogation API; audit/provenance API; webhook/event stream; mobile SDK; connector SDK; synthetic claim sandbox; line-of-business pack interfaces.

## Data architecture

Tenant-isolated claim/policy/party stores; claim evidence graph; immutable original artifacts; derived document/media features; estimate/provider data; task/workflow events; communication log; decision/authority ledger; payment/recovery refs; model/rule versions; audit/provenance; retention/legal-hold state; region/residency; secrets separated; backups and recovery.

## Data moat

Potential moat: de-identified/authorized claim process patterns, damage/estimate evaluation corpus, provider performance, workflow reliability, fraud-indicator evaluation, line-of-business ontologies and verified outcome-to-evidence relationships. Never depend on unauthorized pooling of identifiable claimant data or confidential insurer claim histories.

## IP

Claim evidence graph; multimodal damage-to-estimate linkage; claim workflow ontology; line-specific packs; evidence/provenance model; severity/fraud calibration framework; estimate variance engine; CAT orchestration; QA/leakage analytics; claims evaluation suite.

## Monetization

Per claim; per FNOL; per document/media analysis; per active claim; per adjuster/user; API usage; enterprise subscription; line-of-business modules; private deployment; white-label/OEM; managed claims infrastructure; outcome-linked admin efficiency/recovery only where lawful and contractually appropriate. No revenue promise.

## Packaging

FNOL/triage; document/media intelligence; estimate/provider; fraud/investigation support; claim workflow/communications; payment/recovery; QA/analytics; CAT edition; full claims OS; enterprise/private; API/OEM.

## Distribution

Insurance core/software partnerships; TPAs/MGAs; enterprise insurer procurement; claims service networks; repair/restoration technology; developer/API channels; implementation partners. No outreach authorized now.

## Acquisition automation

Future inbound qualification may identify line of business, claim volume, core system, evidence mix and desired automation. It may not solicit, bind insurance, promise outcomes, negotiate contracts or process real claims without authorization.

## Customer lifecycle

Security/regulatory review → line-of-business mapping → integration assessment → synthetic/sandbox calibration → controlled shadow/pilot → adjuster/human-review calibration → limited rollout → QA/fairness/performance monitoring → expansion → renewal/export/offboarding.

## Support / customer success

Claim/integration failures; media/document errors; estimate/provider issues; workflow queues; communication status; payment/reconciliation; model explanations; incidents. Success measures cycle time, automation rate, adjuster burden, QA, customer service and leakage metrics where validated—not guaranteed claim outcomes or savings.

## Automation maximum / human-intervention minimum

Automate FNOL extraction, data validation, evidence ingestion, document classification, image/video feature extraction, routine tasking, status communications, provider eligibility, estimate comparison, deadline tracking, reconciliation and low-risk routing. Retain qualified humans for consequential coverage/liability/fraud/medical/legal/settlement/reserve/payment decisions unless explicitly authorized deterministic rules exist.

## Operations / administration

Insurer/line configuration; policy/product mapping; provider networks; integration credentials; claim queues; model/rule versions; authority matrices; communications templates; QA sampling; security/privacy; incident response; billing; support; backup/recovery; vendor management; regulatory change packs; customer offboarding.

## Security

High-sensitivity PII/financial/medical-adjacent data: encryption; tenant isolation; SSO/MFA; least privilege; claims-role separation; secrets vault; JIT access; secure media upload; malware scanning; DLP; model/tool egress controls; signed artifacts; payment-action protection; immutable audit; key rotation; vulnerability management; incident response.

## Privacy

Minimize claimant/third-party/medical data; purpose limitation; consent/contact preferences; retention; region/residency; access accounting; data subject rights where applicable; sensitive-data segmentation; no customer claim data training by default; cross-tenant isolation; redaction/tokenization; privacy impact assessments.

## Compliance

Architecture must adapt to insurance regulation, unfair-claims-practice rules, privacy/security, consumer communication, payment, recordkeeping, catastrophe/emergency rules, line-of-business requirements and jurisdiction-specific obligations. Actual insurer/TPA responsibilities and licensed activities require qualified legal/compliance validation.

## Legal

Policy/contract interpretation boundaries; adjuster licensing; claims handling regulations; communications; fraud reporting; medical/privacy rules; payment authority; subrogation; litigation holds; data/vendor licensing; record retention; consumer complaints; AI/model governance requirements where applicable. Platform support does not transfer insurer legal responsibility.

## Abuse / misuse

Prevent fabricated claims/evidence, image manipulation, duplicate claims, identity fraud, provider collusion, claimant discrimination, improper surveillance, unsupported fraud accusations, unauthorized claim denial/lowballing, payment diversion, adjuster credential abuse, evidence deletion/tampering and prompt/document attacks.

## Reliability

Claim state machine; idempotent external effects; durable queues; retries/dead letters; duplicate protection; payment reconciliation; model/rule version pinning; source freshness; manual fallback; safe degradation; no unattended adverse action during outage; backup/restore; CAT load shedding; disaster recovery.

## Observability

FNOL volume; claim inventory; queue age; assignment time; cycle time; evidence completeness; document/media confidence; estimate variance; severity calibration; fraud-indicator rates; manual overrides; authority escalations; payment/recovery status; CAT load; core/provider health; model cost; security/privacy events; incident state.

## Incident response

Critical incidents: cross-claim/tenant exposure, mass wrong routing/coverage support, unsupported fraud labeling, payment diversion/duplicate payment, corrupted evidence, compromised adjuster/provider credentials, biased model behavior, catastrophic outage during event. Stop affected automation, preserve evidence, identify affected claims, force human review, reconcile external actions/payments, notify authorized stakeholders, rollback model/rule/config and postmortem.

## Testing

Synthetic/consented claim corpus; FNOL extraction; policy schema; document/media classification; damage/estimate benchmarks; fraud-indicator calibration; authority routing; communication safety; payment idempotency/reconciliation; cross-tenant isolation; privacy; bias/fairness; prompt/image manipulation; core/provider outages; CAT load; disaster recovery; version regression.

## Brain evaluations

Evidence citation; claim summary accuracy; damage/estimate analysis; triage/severity calibration; fraud-indicator precision/recall and explanation; unsupported adverse conclusion rate; policy data handling; escalation; fairness; leakage; tool authorization; communication quality; source faithfulness.

## Deployment

Isolated dev/test/staging/production; line/product configuration; signed releases; model/rule candidate versions; feature flags; canary by insurer/line/claim segment; rollback; private/single-tenant options; region controls; protected payment/action channels. No production deployment authorized now.

## Scale

Single low-risk workflow → one insurance line → multi-line insurer → TPA/MGA network → catastrophe-scale operations → embedded claims infrastructure. Scale media processing, claim queues, communication, provider routing and analytics independently.

## Performance

FNOL/claim status interactive; media/document processing near-real-time or asynchronous; CAT ingestion high-throughput; payment/reconciliation deterministic. Avoid blocking emergency claim intake on optional AI services.

## Cost

Model inference; photo/video processing; OCR/transcription; data enrichment; geospatial/weather/vendor APIs; storage/retention; communications; integrations; security/compliance/support. Track cost per claim/workflow/media item and internalization candidates; no spend authorized now.

## Financial metrics

ARR/MRR if later real; revenue per claim/module/API; gross margin; model/media/vendor cost per claim; implementation/support cost; retention/expansion; automation rate; cycle time; leakage/recovery metrics when validated. No test revenue.

## Moat

Claims evidence graph; multimodal damage/evaluation corpus; line packs; provider/estimate intelligence; workflow reliability; CAT scale; QA/leakage patterns; insurer trust and integrations.

## Network effects

Non-private benefits from wider provider/repair integrations, de-identified benchmark ranges and evaluation data. Private claim/claimant data stays isolated unless explicitly authorized.

## Platform

Can become claims operating infrastructure coordinating intake, evidence, people, providers, decisions, payments, recovery, analytics and external systems.

## White label / OEM

Insurers, TPAs, MGAs and insurance software vendors may embed modules/APIs. Carrier policy/authority, claims identity and audit remain explicit.

## Internationalization

Insurance products, claims regulation, languages, currencies, tax, repair networks, medical systems, catastrophe response and privacy differ by jurisdiction; require country/line packs and local validation.

## Accessibility

Accessible claimant and adjuster experiences; keyboard/screen-reader support; text scaling; accessible media alternatives; non-color-only statuses; plain-language communications; alternate channels for document/evidence submission.

## Mobile

Strong fit for FNOL, photo/video capture, claimant status, adjuster field work, approvals and provider coordination. Secure device/session, offline capture, upload integrity, accessibility and location permission controls required.

## Voice

Call FNOL transcription, adjuster note dictation and status automation may be useful with consent/recording-law controls. Voice outputs never replace source recordings/transcripts and cannot authorize protected decisions by themselves.

## Multimodal

Core capability: photos, video, documents, voice, scans, maps, estimates and sensor/telemetry data. Every extracted fact or damage inference retains source location/time/confidence and review state.

## Marketplace

Potential certified repair/restoration/provider connectors, line packs, data enrichments and workflow modules. Third parties require permission scopes, security, quality and contractual review.

## Developer ecosystem

Claims/FNOL/evidence/media/estimate/payment/recovery APIs; mobile SDK; synthetic claim sandbox; connector SDK; line-pack interface; event/webhook system; evaluation fixtures; versioning/deprecation/certification.

## Partners

Core claims vendors; insurers/TPAs/MGAs; repair/restoration networks; payment providers; weather/geospatial/vehicle/property data vendors; fraud providers; integrators. Planning only, no outreach authorized.

## Training / certification

Claims administrator; adjuster-support user; integration developer; QA reviewer; model/authority administrator; CAT operator; security/privacy/incident training; partner connector certification.

## Community

Future non-sensitive insurer/claims-operations community for workflow patterns, integration feedback and benchmarking methodology. No claimant data or confidential claim files shared.

## Content / knowledge

Line-of-business playbooks; evidence/estimate guides; model/rule explanations; provider integration docs; CAT runbooks; QA/audit guides; claimant communication templates subject to legal review; developer docs; release notes.

## Experimentation

Synthetic/historical consented data; shadow mode; offline model comparisons; controlled pilots; fairness analysis. Never silently alter coverage/settlement/payment/fraud thresholds or protected workflows; pre-defined rollback and human review.

## Continuous improvement

Learn from adjuster overrides, QA findings, provider variance, payment/recovery reconciliation, CAT events and incidents. Update evaluations and compatibility profiles; governed promotion only.

## Spinoffs

FNOL API; damage intelligence; estimate comparison; provider routing; subrogation intelligence; CAT orchestration; claim QA could become standalone products or companies only after classification/new-company test.

## Cross-sell

Adjacent companies: fraud detection, document intelligence, payments/reconciliation, e-discovery/litigation evidence, geospatial risk, workflow automation, KYC/identity, customer communications. Keep separate projects.

## Bundling

FNOL/triage; evidence/damage; estimate/provider; fraud/investigation support; payment/recovery; QA/analytics; CAT; full claims OS; enterprise/private/OEM.

## Failures

Wrong policy/claimant; duplicate claim; missing exposure; corrupted evidence; manipulated image; bad damage inference; estimate mismatch; false fraud signal; biased routing; provider error; missed deadline; communication error; reserve/settlement support error; duplicate/wrong payment; subrogation miss; CAT overload; core-system drift.

## Edge cases

Multiple policies/coverages; multiple claimants/exposures; partial loss; total loss; prior damage; pre-existing condition; disputed causation; catastrophe; multiple currencies/countries; salvage; deductible erosion; policy endorsements; late notice; reopening; litigation; minors/guardians; third-party claims; uninsured/underinsured; subrogation complexity; repair supplements; fraud rings; provider insolvency.

## Kill / safe mode

Per insurer/line/model/agent/provider/payment/integration kill; freeze adverse or payment-support automation; force manual handling; read-only claim status; disable suspect fraud/damage model; quarantine media; revoke credentials; rollback rule/model/config; CAT emergency mode; preserve evidence/audit.

## Exit / portability

Export claim records, evidence, derived findings, task/communication history, decisions/authority, estimates, payments/recoveries, model/rule versions and audit trail in documented formats; revoke integrations; retain/delete per law/contract.

## Scale vision

FNOL/triage point solution → multi-module claims suite → insurer/TPA claims OS → catastrophe-scale platform → embedded claims infrastructure across insurance ecosystems.

## Autonomous mature state

Routine intake, evidence processing, classification, task routing, provider coordination, status updates, estimate comparison, QA and reconciliation run automatically. Authorized human adjusters/compliance/legal owners retain consequential coverage, fraud, liability, reserve, settlement and payment authority. All recommendations/actions remain sourced, versioned and auditable.

## Command Center dependencies

First-class project/button/progress/pages; Brain/Agent factories; Capability/Integration registries; identity/tenant; data governance; security/privacy/authorization; multimodal/document intelligence; workflow/queues; payments/reconciliation protection; provider/integration registry; testing/evaluation/fairness; observability/incident/recovery; resource/financial governors; audit/provenance; approval/Needs Me; versioning.

## Retrofit risk

If Command Center cannot isolate claims/tenants, separate recommendations from binding decisions, track authority levels, preserve multimodal provenance, protect payments and support CAT-scale degradation/recovery, later claims infrastructure would require unsafe retrofits.

## Phased roadmap

Phase 0 architecture/synthetic claim corpus → Phase 1 FNOL/policy/claim/evidence → Phase 2 document/media/triage → Phase 3 estimate/provider/workflow → Phase 4 fraud/severity/QA analytics → Phase 5 payment/recovery/subrogation → Phase 6 CAT/multi-line enterprise → Phase 7 API/OEM/private → Phase 8 governed continuous improvement/internalization.

## Reuse candidates

Identity/tenant; document/media extraction; evidence/provenance; workflow/queues; communications; provider registry; payments/reconciliation; graph; geospatial/event adapters; audit; observability; incident/recovery; evaluation; versioning; approval/authority engine.

## Proven capability dependencies

Shared models/services require claim-line-specific fit, fairness, security, evidence and authority testing. Critical payment, identity, evidence and adverse-decision support components require proof maturity, staged rollout and rollback/fork options.

## Company-specific capabilities

Claims ontology; policy/coverage/exposure semantics; line packs; damage/estimate intelligence; adjuster authority model; CAT orchestration; reserve/settlement support evaluations; subrogation/recovery; claim-specific fairness/safety corpus.

## External dependencies to internalize

Generic candidates: document/media understanding, workflow, communications, provider integration, reconciliation, evaluation, geospatial adapters. Proprietary insurance core, repair estimating, weather/vehicle/property and licensed fraud datasets may remain external with portability/provenance.

## Blast-radius requirements

Original section Business identity (source line 11):
Purpose: digitize and intelligently coordinate insurance claim workflows from first notice through evidence, triage, investigation support, estimating, communications, settlement support, payment workflow, subrogation, closure and reopening while preserving insurer policy, regulatory, contractual and human decision boundaries.

Core problem: claims operations combine policy interpretation, claimant identity, incident evidence, documents, photos/video, estimates, providers, fraud indicators, reserves, communications, legal/regulatory deadlines, payment and recovery. Fragmented systems and manual handoffs slow resolution and create inconsistent service, leakage and audit risk.

Value proposition: an evidence-centered claims operating layer that automates intake, normalization, document/media understanding, workflow routing, routine task execution, provider coordination, quality checks and analytics while keeping consequential coverage, fraud, liability, settlement and payment authority with properly authorized insurer personnel or rules.

Non-goal: not an autonomous insurer, adjuster, attorney or medical evaluator; not a system that independently denies claims, accuses fraud, makes binding settlement decisions or pays money without explicit policy and authorization.

# Company 107 — Rights, Royalties & Licensing Operations Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:107`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:107`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-107-v2.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Roadmap conformance:** EXHAUSTIVE 28-PASS / A–BZ MAPPED; saturation subject to portfolio reverse-map reconciliation  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no rights registration, license grant, royalty payment, legal clearance, contract execution, infringement claim, creator outreach, customer onboarding, spending, deployment or public launch.  
**First-class project requirement:** independent Command Center project button, independently computed percentage, independent project pages, Brain/Agent/service state, evidence/checkpoints, Needs Me, incidents, approvals, dependencies and lifecycle.

## Business identity

Purpose: track ownership, rights, licenses, permitted/prohibited uses, territories, windows, exclusivity, sublicensing, usage, revenue allocation, royalty obligations, recoupment, statements, reconciliation, underpayment and audit for intellectual property and digital content.

Core problem: rights and royalty operations are fragmented across contracts, spreadsheets, collecting societies, labels/publishers, distributors, platforms, agencies, content systems and accounting. Ownership may be fractional and layered; permissions vary by territory, medium, term and exclusivity; usage arrives in inconsistent formats; deductions/recoupment complicate calculations; rights expire, conflict, transfer and fragment over time.

Value proposition: a versioned rights graph and royalty operating layer that connects contracts, ownership, permissions, usage and money with evidence, explains every allocation, alerts on conflicts/expiry/underpayment and supports clearance/licensing workflows without pretending to replace legal review.

Non-goal: not autonomous legal counsel; not a system that independently grants rights, represents disputed ownership as settled, pays royalties, signs licenses, waives rights or asserts infringement without authorized human/legal process.

## Complete product tree

Rights Registry; Works/Assets Registry; Parties/Contributor Registry; Ownership/Split Registry; Chain-of-Title Graph; Rights Graph; Territory/Window Matrix; Exclusivity Manager; Media/Format Rights Manager; Language Rights; Derivative Rights; Adaptation Rights; Synchronization Rights; Mechanical/Performance Rights Support; Publishing Rights Support; Master/Recording Rights Support; Image/Footage Rights; Name/Image/Likeness Rights; Voice/Digital Replica Rights; AI Training/Model-Use Rights Registry; Merchandising Rights; Live/Event Rights; Brand/Trademark License Support; Patent/Technology License Support; Sublicensing Rights Manager; Contract Ingestion; Contract Term Extraction; Contract Version/Amendment Manager; Obligation Calendar; License Database; License Request Intake; Clearance Workbench; Rights Availability Checker; Conflict Detector; License Offer/Draft Support; Approval Workflow; Option/Renewal Manager; Minimum Guarantee Manager; Advance/Recoupment Ledger; Escalator/Tier Rules; Usage Ingestion; Platform/Distributor Statement Ingestion; Usage Normalization; Identifier Matching; Work/Recording/Asset Matching; Royalty Rule Engine; Royalty Calculator; Split Allocation; Currency/FX Handling; Deductions/Reserves; Recoupment; Statement Generator; Payee Ledger; Payment Instruction Preparation; Tax/Withholding Data Interface; Reconciliation; Underpayment Detection; Missing Usage Detection; Audit Support; Dispute/Exception Case Management; Attribution/Credit Manager; Cue/Metadata Support; Creator/Rightsholder Portal; Licensee Portal; Rights Expiry/Renewal Monitor; Takedown/Restriction Support; Territory/Window Enforcement Signals; Usage Authorization API; Rights Availability API; Royalty API; Metadata/Identifier API; Enterprise Multi-Catalog Console; White-Label/OEM; Private Deployment; Industry Packs.

## Complete feature tree

Work/asset IDs; ISRC/ISWC/ISBN/DOI/UPC/internal IDs where applicable; title/alternate title; version/edition; contributor/party; role; ownership share; administration share; rights type; rights holder; chain-of-title evidence; territory; language; media/format; platform/channel; term/start/end; window; exclusivity; sublicensing permission; derivative/adaptation scope; restrictions; approval rights; usage caps; minimum guarantee; advance; recoupment pool; royalty base; rate; tier/escalator; deductions; reserves; tax/withholding refs; currency; exchange rate; statement period; usage unit; revenue; allocation; payment status; dispute; contract/source/version; amendment/supersession; approval status; confidence; human decision; audit/provenance.

## Complete customer tree

Music labels; music publishers; artists/managers; composers/songwriters; rights administrators; PRO/CMO-adjacent administrators where lawful; film/TV studios; production companies; distributors; streaming platforms; podcast networks; book publishers; authors/agencies; game studios; media companies; photo/footage libraries; stock media platforms; creator businesses; sports/entertainment licensors; brand licensing organizations; merchandise companies; agencies; museums/archives; education/research publishers; enterprise IP/legal teams; patent/technology licensors; marketplaces; collecting/royalty service providers; rights-tech vendors.

## Complete vertical tree

Recorded music; music publishing; film/TV; streaming; podcasts; books/ebooks/audiobooks; games; photography; stock footage; creator/influencer content; sports/media rights; brand/trademark licensing; merchandising; archives; education; software/technology licensing; patent licensing administration; AI training/data/model rights; voice/digital replica/likeness; live/events. Each vertical requires rights ontology, contract patterns, identifiers, usage feeds, payment rules and legal/jurisdiction packs.

## Specialized Brain capability tree

The Rights & Royalties Brain must KNOW rights categories, ownership, chain of title, licensing, territories, windows, exclusivity, options/renewals, usage, royalty structures, advances/recoupment, deductions, statements, identifiers and vertical-specific contract concepts. It must UNDERSTAND contract and asset context; CLASSIFY rights/terms/usage/obligations; REASON about availability, conflicts, ownership chains and royalty formulas; PLAN evidence collection and licensing/statement workflows; PREDICT revenue/expiry/conflict/underpayment risk as assistive analytics; FORECAST obligations and payment workload; OPTIMIZE catalog administration and reconciliation; RECOMMEND actions with cited terms; VERIFY calculations/source/version; EXPLAIN every allocation/constraint; ESCALATE disputed ownership, ambiguous legal terms, protected licensing and high-impact payment decisions.

The Brain must separately represent contract text, extracted term, inferred interpretation, approved legal/business interpretation, ownership claim, disputed claim, usage record, accounting fact and calculated royalty.

## Brain architecture

Brain Factory base + rights/royalties domain pack + vertical packs + contract clause/term ontology + rights/ownership graph + temporal/territorial entitlement engine + deterministic royalty calculation engine + usage/revenue normalization layer + provenance/evidence ledger + human legal/business approval policy.

Memory is tenant/catalog/matter isolated. Private contracts and royalty statements do not become cross-customer memory by default. Versioned interpretations remain linked to the source clause and human approval state.

Evaluations: contract-term extraction; rights availability; territory/window resolution; ownership/split math; recoupment; tier/escalator math; statement reconciliation; identifier matching; underpayment detection; source faithfulness; unsupported legal conclusion rate; cross-tenant leakage; clause ambiguity escalation; prompt/document injection; currency precision; historical reproducibility.

## Complete Agent tree

Catalog Intake Agent; Contract Ingestion Agent; Clause/Term Agent; Chain-of-Title Agent; Ownership/Split Agent; Rights Availability Agent; Conflict Agent; Clearance Agent; Licensing Workflow Agent; Renewal/Option Agent; Metadata/Identifier Agent; Usage Ingestion Agent; Usage Matching Agent; Royalty Calculation Agent; Recoupment Agent; Statement Agent; Reconciliation Agent; Underpayment Agent; Payment Instruction Agent; Tax/Withholding Interface Agent; Attribution/Credit Agent; Rights Enforcement Signal Agent; Dispute/Exception Agent; Audit Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Independent QA Agent.

No agent independently grants rights, makes final legal interpretations, waives claims, issues binding infringement allegations, changes disputed ownership, releases material royalty payments or executes licenses without explicit authority.

## Deterministic / non-agent services

Decimal/fixed-point royalty math; split validation; percentage sum checks; tier/escalator calculators; recoupment ledger; minimum-guarantee tracking; currency/FX conversion with source/time; identifier normalization; fuzzy asset matching; contract/date/window calendars; territory hierarchy; rights-rule evaluation where codified; usage aggregation; statement normalization; double-entry ledger interfaces; tax/withholding calculations where rules are explicitly encoded and validated; document hashing; audit logging; idempotency; payment reconciliation; retention; versioning; backup/restore.

## Input tree

Contracts; amendments; side letters; schedules; ownership agreements; assignments; licenses; metadata; works/assets; contributor data; splits; identifiers; territory definitions; usage reports; streaming/distribution statements; sales/download/view/stream/performance units; gross/net revenue; deductions; returns/reserves; advances; minimum guarantees; expenses; FX rates; tax/withholding data; payment records; cue sheets; platform metadata; takedown/restriction notices; human approvals; disputes/audit records.

## Output tree

Rights graph; chain-of-title view; ownership/split table; availability/clearance result; conflict/expiry alert; contract-term summary; obligation calendar; license workflow packet; usage normalization/match report; royalty calculation; recoupment statement; payee statement; payment instruction candidate; reconciliation variance; underpayment/missing-usage alert; audit package; dispute case; attribution/credit output; territory/window enforcement signal; API response; human-review task.

## Workflow tree

Authorize catalog/customer → ingest assets/parties/contracts → preserve originals → extract terms → human/legal approve ambiguous interpretations → build ownership/rights graph → validate splits/chain of title → ingest license terms/obligations → monitor expiry/options/renewals → ingest and normalize usage/revenue → match usage to assets/rights/parties → calculate royalties/recoupment/deductions deterministically → reconcile statements/payments → route exceptions/underpayments/disputes → prepare approved payment instructions → issue statements through authorized process → retain evidence → audit and update for amendments/transfers/new usage.

## Integration tree

DAM/MAM/CMS; music distribution; streaming/platform reports; publishing systems; film/TV rights systems; book publishing platforms; game/content systems; ERP/accounting; payment systems; tax systems; CRM; contract lifecycle management; e-signature references where authorized; PRO/CMO/distributor feeds; metadata/identifier registries; cloud storage; document management; SSO; data warehouse/BI; ticketing/dispute systems; SIEM; legal systems.

## API / developer ecosystem

Rights Registry API; Asset/Party API; Ownership/Split API; Rights Availability API; License API; Usage Ingest API; Usage Match API; Royalty Calculation API; Statement API; Reconciliation API; Payment Instruction API; Audit/Provenance API; Metadata/Identifier API; webhooks/events; connector SDK; vertical pack SDK; synthetic catalog/contract sandbox; versioned schemas.

## Data architecture

Tenant-isolated catalog/party/contract stores; immutable source contract artifacts; extracted/approved term store; temporal rights graph; ownership/chain-of-title graph; usage event lake; normalized statement store; royalty ledger; recoupment ledger; payment/reconciliation refs; disputes/exceptions; audit/provenance ledger; version/effective-date state; secrets separated; residency/retention; backup/recovery.

## Data moat

Potential moat: rights ontology, contract extraction/evaluation corpus, identifier/usage matching quality, royalty-rule compatibility, chain-of-title/rights graph, statement normalization adapters and de-identified authorized reconciliation benchmarks. Never pool private contracts, unpublished catalog economics or rightsholder financial data without authorization.

## IP

Temporal rights graph; rights availability compiler; contract-to-rights parser; chain-of-title evidence model; royalty formula DSL/engine; recoupment ledger; usage matching; statement normalization; underpayment detector; rights conflict/expiry engine; AI-training/digital-likeness rights model; evaluation corpus.

## Monetization

Per asset/work; per contract/license; per usage record; per statement; percentage/fee on administered royalties only if legally/contractually appropriate; subscription; seats; enterprise catalog license; API usage; private deployment; white-label/OEM; managed rights administration; audit/reconciliation module. No revenue promise.

## Packaging

capabilities: The Rights & Royalties Brain must KNOW rights categories, ownership, chain of title, licensing, territories, windows, exclusivity, options/renewals, usage, royalty structures, advances/recoupment, deductions, statements, identifiers and vertical-specific contract concepts. It must UNDERSTAND contract and asset context
REASON about availability, conflicts, ownership chains and royalty formulas
PLAN evidence collection and licensing/statement workflows
PREDICT revenue/expiry/conflict/underpayment risk as assistive analytics

ESCALATE disputed ownership, ambiguous legal terms, protected licensing and high-impact payment decisions. The Brain must separately represent contract text, extracted term, inferred interpretation, approved legal/business interpretation, ownership claim, disputed claim, usage record, accounting fact and calculated royalty.

Independent QA Agent. No agent independently grants rights, makes final legal interpretations, waives claims, issues binding infringement allegations, changes disputed ownership, releases material royalty payments or executes licenses without explicit authority.
